title: Accented, CJK and emoji characters render at their width and the cursor stays aligned
why: CJK and emoji take two cells. If the terminal (the app's view or the daemon's screen) gives one a different width than programs do, every cursor move after it lands in the wrong cell: text after the characters is misplaced and line editing garbles. The bar is placed by an absolute cursor move after the wide characters and must touch the last one; a prompt of wide characters must keep an in-line edit in place.

steps.title: the shell runs in a UTF-8 locale
W, two CJK characters (2 cells each), an emoji (2 cells) and an accented letter fill 8 cells; the bar moved to column 9 touches them
the prompt is now CJK and an emoji
an edit after a wide prompt lands in place, on screen and in the command
